"""Track-side infrastructure models for a small tram junction.

These classes represent the physical layer that the interlocking logic
in :mod:`interlocking` reasons about: track circuits (occupancy
detection) and points (motorised switches).
"""


class PointLockedError(Exception):
    """Raised when an attempt is made to move a point that cannot move."""


class TrackCircuit:
    """A single length of track fitted with continuity detection.

    A track circuit reports whether a vehicle (or anything else that
    shorts the running rails, e.g. a broken rail) is present on the
    section it covers.
    """

    def __init__(self, circuit_id: str, name: str):
        self.circuit_id = circuit_id
        self.name = name
        self._occupied = False

    @property
    def occupied(self) -> bool:
        return self._occupied

    def set_occupied(self, occupied: bool) -> None:
        self._occupied = occupied

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        state = "OCCUPIED" if self._occupied else "clear"
        return f"TrackCircuit({self.circuit_id}, {state})"


class Point:
    """A motorised switch that can be set to NORMAL or REVERSE.

    A point can only be thrown while the track circuit covering its
    blades is clear -- moving the blades under a tram would derail
    it. Once a route locks a point, ``locked`` is set True by the
    interlocking and further throws are refused until the route that
    locked it is released.
    """

    NORMAL = "normal"
    REVERSE = "reverse"

    def __init__(self, point_id: str, name: str, blade_circuit: TrackCircuit):
        self.point_id = point_id
        self.name = name
        self.blade_circuit = blade_circuit
        self.position = Point.NORMAL
        self.locked = False

    def throw(self, position: str) -> None:
        if position not in (Point.NORMAL, Point.REVERSE):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown point position {position!r}")
        if self.locked:
            raise PointLockedError(
                f"point {self.point_id} is route-locked and cannot be thrown"
            )
        if self.blade_circuit.occupied:
            raise PointLockedError(
                f"point {self.point_id} blades are occupied, refusing to throw"
            )
        self.position = position

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        lock = "locked" if self.locked else "free"
        return f"Point({self.point_id}, {self.position}, {lock})"

"""Ties track circuits, points, and interlocking logic together, and
derives the aspect each entry signal should display to tram drivers.

Aspects follow a simplified two-block speed-signalling scheme:

* RED    -- stop; the route is not set, or the section immediately
  ahead of the signal is occupied.
* YELLOW -- proceed with caution, be ready to stop; only the section
  immediately ahead is guaranteed clear.
* GREEN  -- proceed; the section immediately ahead and the one after
  it are both clear.

Sections further down the route than that are not this signal's
concern -- they are covered by the route locking itself (a route
cannot be set at all while any of its track circuits are occupied)
and, on a longer route, by the next signal along.
"""

from typing import Dict

from track_model import Point, TrackCircuit
from interlocking import Interlocking, Route, RouteRequestError

RED, YELLOW, GREEN = "RED", "YELLOW", "GREEN"


class SignalController:
    def __init__(self, interlocking: Interlocking):
        self.interlocking = interlocking
        self.aspects: Dict[str, str] = {
            route.entry_signal: RED for route in interlocking.routes.values()
        }

    def request(self, route_id: str) -> None:
        """Ask the interlocking to set a route and refresh aspects."""
        self.interlocking.request_route(route_id)
        self.refresh()

    def clear_train(self, route_id: str) -> None:
        """Release a route once a tram has fully cleared it."""
        if self.interlocking.route_is_fully_clear(route_id):
            self.interlocking.release_route(route_id)
        self.refresh()

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        """Recompute every entry signal's aspect from current state."""
        for route_id, route in self.interlocking.routes.items():
            signal = route.entry_signal

            if not self.interlocking.is_locked(route_id):
                self.aspects[signal] = RED
                continue

            first_id = route.track_circuit_ids[0]
            if self.interlocking.track_circuits[first_id].occupied:
                self.aspects[signal] = RED
                continue

            if len(route.track_circuit_ids) > 1:
                second_id = route.track_circuit_ids[1]
                second_clear = not self.interlocking.track_circuits[second_id].occupied
            else:
                second_clear = True

            self.aspects[signal] = GREEN if second_clear else YELLOW

    def aspect_for(self, signal: str) -> str:
        return self.aspects.get(signal, RED)


def build_demo_interlocking() -> Interlocking:
    """Build a two-route junction: Elm Street and Oak Avenue converge
    through a single point onto the shared approach to City Centre.
    """
    tc_elm = TrackCircuit("TC1_ELM", "Elm Street approach")
    tc_oak = TrackCircuit("TC1_OAK", "Oak Avenue approach")
    tc_junction = TrackCircuit("TC2_JCN", "Junction")
    tc_city = TrackCircuit("TC3_CITY", "City Centre approach")

    point = Point("P1", "Elm/Oak convergence point", blade_circuit=tc_junction)

    track_circuits = {
        tc.circuit_id: tc for tc in (tc_elm, tc_oak, tc_junction, tc_city)
    }
    points = {point.point_id: point}

    route_a = Route(
        route_id="A_ELM_TO_CITY",
        entry_signal="SIG_ELM",
        exit_signal="SIG_CITY",
        track_circuit_ids=["TC1_ELM", "TC2_JCN", "TC3_CITY"],
        point_positions={"P1": Point.NORMAL},
        conflicts={"B_OAK_TO_CITY"},
    )
    route_b = Route(
        route_id="B_OAK_TO_CITY",
        entry_signal="SIG_OAK",
        exit_signal="SIG_CITY",
        track_circuit_ids=["TC1_OAK", "TC2_JCN", "TC3_CITY"],
        point_positions={"P1": Point.REVERSE},
        conflicts={"A_ELM_TO_CITY"},
    )

    routes = {route_a.route_id: route_a, route_b.route_id: route_b}
    return Interlocking(track_circuits, points, routes)


def main() -> None:
    interlocking = build_demo_interlocking()
    controller = SignalController(interlocking)

    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_ELM") == RED
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_OAK") == RED
    print("Both approaches start at danger: OK")

    controller.request("A_ELM_TO_CITY")
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_ELM") == GREEN
    print("Route A set, SIG_ELM shows GREEN")

    try:
        controller.request("B_OAK_TO_CITY")
        raise AssertionError("expected conflicting route to be refused")
    except RouteRequestError as exc:
        print(f"Route B correctly refused: {exc}")

    tc = interlocking.track_circuits
    tc["TC2_JCN"].set_occupied(True)
    controller.refresh()
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_ELM") == YELLOW
    print("Tram has entered the junction, SIG_ELM steps down to YELLOW")

    tc["TC2_JCN"].set_occupied(False)
    tc["TC3_CITY"].set_occupied(True)
    controller.refresh()
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_ELM") == GREEN
    print("Tram now on the city approach, SIG_ELM returns to GREEN")

    tc["TC3_CITY"].set_occupied(False)
    controller.clear_train("A_ELM_TO_CITY")
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_ELM") == RED
    assert not interlocking.is_locked("A_ELM_TO_CITY")
    print("Tram has cleared the route; route A released")

    controller.request("B_OAK_TO_CITY")
    assert controller.aspect_for("SIG_OAK") == GREEN
    assert interlocking.points["P1"].position == Point.REVERSE
    print("Route B now sets across the junction with the point reversed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
